description: Godot 4.3 HTML5 export scaffold — project.godot, a minimal scene with a label + sprite, a _ready/_process script, and an export_presets.cfg pointed at exports/web/. Open in Godot 4.3+, press Export → HTML5, ship the resulting dist. Foundation for Godot browser games, prototypes, and jam entries.

buildHints.whenToUse: Godot-authored games or interactive content targeting the browser. This scaffold gives you the project skeleton and export preset; you still open Godot 4.3+ to iterate and to actually export. Pick bevy-web for Rust-first games or threejs-game for JavaScript-first 3D content.
firstSteps: Install Godot 4.3+ from godotengine.org (or via `brew install --cask godot` on macOS). Command-line builds additionally require the matching Web export templates — download via Editor → Manage Export Templates.
Open the project: `godot --editor .` from the project root, or drag `project.godot` onto the Godot executable.
Inspect `scenes/main.tscn` — one Node2D root with a Sprite2D and a Label; `scripts/main.gd` attaches to the root and drives a simple _process animation. Press F5 to run in the editor.
Export to web: Project → Export → select `Web` → Export Project. Output lands in `exports/web/` as `index.html` + `index.js` + `index.wasm` + `index.pck`. Ship that directory to any static host.
Headless CI export: `godot --headless --export-release 'Web' exports/web/index.html` from the project root once export templates are installed.
gotchas: Godot 4 HTML5 builds require SharedArrayBuffer, which browsers only expose when the page is served with `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin` and `Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp`. Without these headers the export loads to a blank canvas — configure your static host (Cloudflare Pages, Vercel, nginx) to emit them for the exports/web/ directory.
Web export templates must match the Godot editor version exactly (e.g. 4.3-stable editor needs 4.3-stable templates). Downloading a `dev` template for a `stable` editor silently fails at export time.
The `.godot/` directory is editor-generated cache — do NOT commit it. The supplied .gitignore excludes it.

Godot's HTML5 threading requires WebAssembly threads, which are behind the COOP/COEP gate above AND require the browser to have threads enabled (all modern browsers do, but some mobile browsers in lockdown modes don't).
Audio autoplay is blocked in every browser until the user interacts — wire audio start to a click/keypress or the first frame will have no sound.

Export presets live in `export_presets.cfg` and are version-controlled; they reference absolute paths in your editor on first save — the supplied preset uses relative paths (`exports/web/index.html`) to keep the repo portable.
architectureNotes: Scenes are the primary unit of composition — prefer many small scenes instanced into a parent over one god-scene.
Attach scripts to scene roots only when a node truly owns state; pure utility logic belongs in autoloads (singletons) configured in project.godot.
For web builds specifically, preload assets aggressively — Godot streams from the .pck but first-touch latency on large scenes is visible.

placeholders.description: Main scene with a Node2D root, a centered Sprite2D using the default icon, and a Label. Replace with the real game scene; keep the top-level Node2D if other scenes attach the same `main.gd` script.
GDScript attached to the Node2D root — _ready prints engine version, _process rotates the sprite. Replace the process logic with real input handling and game-loop systems.
